_comment: Hand-logged mentions that no free feed can reach. Google News does not index
audio, so podcast, radio and video appearances are invisible to the
site:-scoped queries in growth_pull.py no matter how many outlets we
whitelist. The 21 Aug 2026 mentions audit found a dozen such appearances
already on the record and uncounted; seeding them here means the dashboard
reflects what is actually known rather than only what a crawler can find.
Going forward, VC_VOICES in growth_pull.py catches new appearances
automatically wherever they produce a crawlable page. This file is for the
rest. To add an entry, copy a row and fill it in -- every field except
'note' is required, and 'url' must be a real link a reader can open.
Nothing here is inferred; each row came from the audit with a source URL.
role: 'appearance' (one of ours was on the show) | 'citation' (someone

items.note: Mamdani said he was "quite taken" by a Vital City piece analyzing decades of crime data, and called its clearance-rate analysis evidence of an "immense crisis."

items.program: The State of Crime in the City
items.note: Identified as founder of Vital City; discussed the crime-data report.

items.program: A Plan to Make Subways Feel Safe Again
items.note: Walked through the subway-safety memo: assaults have replaced robberies as the driver of underground violence.
NY1 said the report could shape the MTA's safety response.

items.program: The Once and Future Greatness of New York City
items.note: On civic culture and getting big ideas into policymaking.

items.program: Zohran Mamdani with Errol Louis: A Conversation on Public Safety
items.note: Co-hosted with Columbia; the candidate's first extended public-safety interview.
Called the new housing issue "great" and summarized its rent-freeze analysis.
On the housing series: Co-op City, design and supply, lessons from Jersey City and Tokyo.

items.program: Patrick Gaspard on Obama, Mamdani and political capital
items.note: Called Vital City an "interesting experiment" giving space to sharp, data-backed arguments.
On What To Do (and Not To Do) About People in Crisis on Streets and Subways.
NY1 called Vital City an urban-policy think tank; on The State of Crime in New York City: 2025 and Beyond.

items.program: Exploring 30 Years of NYC Crime - and What Comes Next
items.note: Demonstrated the Crime Data Explorer to a policy and data audience.
With Deputy Mayor for Community Safety Renita Francois.
